strengths: The paper addresses a clear research interest: transferring information from source code and natural-language summaries into representations of LLVM IR. The anchored encoder and staged contrastive training provide a plausible, understandable approach.

Evaluation spans four tasks and several pretrained baselines. Reported improvements include function-name accuracy of 33.41 versus 29.41 and summarization BLEU-4 of 34.36 versus 32.43. These results suggest potentially useful representations without requiring state-of-the-art performance for publication.
Component ablations, a CodeT5 extension, qualitative examples, and an announced public archive of code, models, and datasets improve the work’s potential usefulness to researchers.
weaknesses: Necessary: Resolve the POJ-104 task definition. Sections 2.3 and 4.2 describe cross-entropy classification among 104 classes, while Section 3.2 and Table 2 specify non-overlapping training, validation, and test labels. An ordinary supervised classifier cannot learn the held-out classes this way. If the experiment actually evaluates retrieval, specify its loss, candidate sets, relevance labels, and metric definitions. This ambiguity affects the principal results and ablations in Tables 3, 7, and 8.

Necessary: Align the binary-analysis claims with the evaluated inputs. The experiments use LLVM IR emitted directly from source, and Figures 7–8 retain informative function, callee, and type names. This does not establish performance on stripped executables or IR recovered from them; those representations are not trivially interchangeable as the footnote suggests. Document compiler settings and symbol handling, and either restrict the claims to this IR setting or supply evidence for the broader setting.

Necessary: Isolate the contribution of interpolation. Primary-only training receives 10 epochs, whereas the full model receives 30 or 70 epochs. Section 5.1 asserts convergence of the shorter ablation without supporting learning curves. Consequently, improvements cannot confidently be attributed to interpolation or the proposed progression. Comparisons with matched training budgets and separate interpolation stages would support these claims; alternatively, narrow the attribution to the combined training procedure.

Necessary: Qualify the conclusion about human versus generated comments. Table 7 reports MAP of 43.78 with generated comments, 42.76 without comments, and 3.11 with human comments, but only on POJ-104. Comparing raw developer comments with generated function summaries confounds authorship with content, coverage, length, and preprocessing. Document extraction and pairing, investigate the dramatic collapse with controlled comparisons, or restrict the conclusion to the particular corpus and configuration. Length distributions alone do not establish the proposed causes.

Necessary: Distinguish textual reconstruction from semantic correctness. BLEU, GLEU, and exact match do not establish functional equivalence of reconstructed programs or usefulness to human analysts. The paper provides no systematic execution-based or human assessment supporting its stronger comprehension claims. Clarify the provenance of summarization references, particularly whether they come from the same CodeT5 generator used during pre-training. Add appropriate semantic validation or narrow the conclusions to the measured textual outcomes.

Necessary: Make the implementation and evaluation descriptions consistent. Algorithm 1 permits interpolating any two modalities, whereas Section 2.4 describes source/comment interpolation; Figure 3 concatenates inputs while Equations 8 and 10 add them. Whether gradients propagate through the targets in Equation 5 is unspecified. Also clarify the separate pre-training and downstream partitions, validation versus test use for generation, and duplicate handling. These details materially affect reproducibility and interpretation.

Necessary: Correct overstatements and numerical reporting. Table 6 gives lower BLEU-4 than GraphCodeBERT (71.14 versus 71.56), while its exact-match advantage is only 0.43 percentage points. Single-seed results without uncertainty estimates do not substantiate claims of consistent, significant superiority. Provide uncertainty evidence or use appropriately descriptive claims. Section 5.1 also mislabels relative percentage decreases as point decreases: removing comments reduces MAF1 by 0.79 points, equivalent to 2.07%.

Optional: Quantitative neighborhood analysis would strengthen the embedding discussion beyond selected t-SNE examples. Streamlining the repeated human-learning analogies would also make room for the missing experimental details.
